     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# A finitely presented Picard representative preserves filtered base colimits
    11	
    12	Representability turns the fixed-base Picard-zero functor into the functor of morphisms to its
    13	representing scheme.  If that scheme is locally of finite presentation, the scheme-theoretic
    14	finite-stage factorization and equality theorems show that this functor preserves the filtered
    15	colimits occurring in `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	
    20	universe u
    21	
    22	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    25	
    26	/-- A locally finitely presented scheme representing `pic0TypeFunctor C` discharges the
    27	fixed-base filtered-colimit residual `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C`. -/
    28	theorem pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit_of_representableBy
    29	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    30	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    31	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    32	    (J : Over (Spec (.of k))) (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    33	    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation J.hom] :
    34	    Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C := by
    35	  intro I _ _ S h_aff hcompact hqs _
    36	  letI : IsConnected I := IsCofiltered.isConnected I
    37	  let D := S ⋙ Over.forget (Spec (.of k))
    38	  let t : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj (Spec (.of k)) :=
    39	    { app := fun i => (S.obj i).hom
    40	      naturality := fun {i j} f => by
    41	        change (S.map f).left ≫ (S.obj j).hom = (S.obj i).hom ≫ 𝟙 _
    42	        rw [Category.comp_id]
    43	        exact Over.w (S.map f) }
    44	  let c : Cone D := (Over.forget (Spec (.of k))).mapCone (limit.cone S)
    45	  have hc : IsLimit c :=
    46	    isLimitOfPreserves (Over.forget (Spec (.of k))) (limit.isLimit S)
    47	  letI {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j) : IsAffineHom (D.map f) := h_aff f
    48	  letI (i : I) : CompactSpace (D.obj i) := hcompact i
    49	  letI (i : I) : QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i) := hqs i
    50	  refine preservesColimit_of_preserves_colimit_cocone
    51	    (K := S.op) (F := pic0TypeFunctor C) (limit.isLimit S).op ?_
    52	  refine Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf' (S.op ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor C)
    53	    ((pic0TypeFunctor C).mapCocone (limit.cone S).op) ?_ ?_
    54	  · intro x
    55	    let a : limit S ⟶ J := rep.homEquiv.symm x
    56	    have ha : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const I).map (a.left ≫ J.hom) := by
    57	      ext i
    58	      change (limit.π S i).left ≫ (S.obj i).hom = a.left ≫ J.hom
    59	      rw [Over.w (limit.π S i), Over.w a]
    60	    obtain ⟨i, g, hg, hgbase⟩ :=
    61	      Scheme.exists_π_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation
    62	        D t J.hom c hc a.left ha
    63	    let g' : S.obj i ⟶ J := Over.homMk g hgbase
    64	    refine ⟨op i, rep.homEquiv g', ?_⟩
    65	    change x = (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (limit.π S i).op (rep.homEquiv g')
    66	    rw [← rep.homEquiv_comp]
    67	    rw [show x = rep.homEquiv a from (rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply x).symm]
    68	    apply congrArg rep.homEquiv
    69	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
    70	    exact hg.symm
    71	  · intro ii x y hxy
    72	    let i := unop ii
    73	    let a : S.obj i ⟶ J := rep.homEquiv.symm x
    74	    let b : S.obj i ⟶ J := rep.homEquiv.symm y
    75	    have ha : t.app i = a.left ≫ J.hom := (Over.w a).symm
    76	    have hb : t.app i = b.left ≫ J.hom := (Over.w b).symm
    77	    have habOver : limit.π S i ≫ a = limit.π S i ≫ b := by
    78	      apply rep.homEquiv.injective
    79	      rw [rep.homEquiv_comp, rep.homEquiv_comp,
    80	        rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply, rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
    81	      exact hxy
    82	    have hab : c.π.app i ≫ a.left = c.π.app i ≫ b.left :=
    83	      congrArg Over.Hom.left habOver
    84	    obtain ⟨j, hji, heq⟩ :=
    85	      Scheme.exists_hom_comp_eq_comp_of_locallyOfFiniteType
    86	        D t J.hom c hc a.left b.left ha hb hab
    87	    refine ⟨op j, hji.op, ?_⟩
    88	    change (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (S.map hji).op x =
    89	      (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (S.map hji).op y
    90	    rw [show x = rep.homEquiv a from (rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply x).symm,
    91	      show y = rep.homEquiv b from (rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply y).symm,
    92	      ← rep.homEquiv_comp, ← rep.homEquiv_comp]
    93	    apply congrArg rep.homEquiv
    94	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
    95	    exact heq
    96	
    97	end AlgebraicGeometry

    52	noncomputable def gluingChartIso

    68	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)

     8	/-!
     9	# Conditional finite-Galois representability for Picard zero
    10	
    11	This is a conditional producer: it descends a finite-level representative only
    12	under the explicitly supplied orbit-in-an-affine-open instance.  It is not the
    13	arbitrary-field representability endpoint.

    16	set_option autoImplicit false

    21	open AlgebraicGeometry
    22	open AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

    29	
    30	/-- Conditional finite-Galois descent of a finite-level Picard-zero representative.
    31	
    32	The orbit-in-an-affine-open instance is the sole extra descent hypothesis here;
    33	this theorem does not claim arbitrary-field representability.
    34	-/
    35	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableBy_finiteGaloisDescent
    36	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
    37	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    38	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    39	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
    40	    {J : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L))}
    41	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange K L).obj C)).RepresentableBy J)
    42	    [((pic0SemilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep).OrbitsInAffineOpen)] :
    43	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
    44	      (AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.StableAffineOpen.gluedQuotientOver
    45	        (pic0SemilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep)) where
    46	  homEquiv {T} :=
    47	    ((StableAffineOpen.gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv
    48	      (pic0SemilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep) T).trans
    49	      (pic0GaloisInvariantEquivGaloisEquivariantOver C rep T).symm).trans
    50	      (pic0GaloisInvariantEquiv (L := L) C T).symm
    51	  homEquiv_comp {T T'} f v := by
    52	    apply (pic0GaloisInvariantEquiv (L := L) C T).injective
    53	    apply (pic0GaloisInvariantEquivGaloisEquivariantOver C rep T).injective
    54	    simp only [Equiv.trans_apply, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
    55	    rw [StableAffineOpen.gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv_precomp]

    57	    rw [pic0GaloisInvariantEquivGaloisEquivariantOver_precomp]
    58	    simp only [Equiv.apply_symm_apply]

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0GaloisInvariantComparison
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# The finite-Galois invariance match for Picard zero
    10	
    11	This module identifies deck invariance of a Picard-zero class with equivariance
    12	of its representing morphism for the canonical semilinear Galois action.
    13	-/
    14	
    15	set_option autoImplicit false
    16	
    17	universe u
    18	
    19	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    20	open AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
    21	
    22	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    23	
    24	noncomputable section
    25	
    26	open Scheme Scheme.PicScheme
    27	
    28	variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    29	
    30	/-! ## The two slice presentations of a deck transformation -/
    31	
    32	/-- The deck transformation of a base-changed test, packaged as a morphism in
    33	the slice over `Spec L`. -/
    34	noncomputable def pic0GalTwistMor
    35	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) (gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
    36	    (pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).obj (baseTest (k' := L) T) ⟶
    37	      baseTest (k' := L) T :=
    38	  Over.homMk (pullbackGalMap K L T.hom gamma)
    39	    (pullbackGalMap_snd K L T.hom gamma)
    40	
    41	@[simp]
    42	theorem pic0GalTwistMor_left
    43	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) (gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
    44	    (pic0GalTwistMor T gamma).left = pullbackGalMap K L T.hom gamma :=
    45	  rfl
    46	
    47	/-- Base change of a morphism of `K`-tests, regarded as a morphism of their
    48	base changes over `Spec L`. -/
    49	noncomputable def pic0GaloisBaseChangeMor
    50	    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T) :
    51	    baseTest (k' := L) T' ⟶ baseTest (k' := L) T :=
    52	  Over.homMk (pullbackBaseChange K L T.hom T'.hom a.left a.w)
    53	    (pullbackBaseChange_snd K L T.hom T'.hom a.left a.w)
    54	
    55	theorem pic0GaloisBaseTestMap_eq_restrict_map
    56	    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T) :
    57	    pic0GaloisBaseTestMap (L := L) a =
    58	      (pic0GaloisRestrictTest (k := K) (L := L)).map
    59	        (pic0GaloisBaseChangeMor (L := L) a) :=
    60	  rfl
    61	
    62	/-- The inverse comparison from a twisted `L`-test to the original test is the
    63	identity on underlying schemes. -/
    64	theorem pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso_inv_app_left
    65	    (gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (D : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L))) :
    66	    ((pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso gamma).inv.app D).left = 𝟙 D.left := by
    67	  have h := congrArg Over.Hom.left
    68	    ((pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso gamma).hom_inv_id_app D)
    69	  rw [Over.comp_left, pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso_hom_app_left] at h
    70	  have hfixed : @Eq (D.left ⟶ D.left)
    71	      (𝟙 D.left ≫ ((pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso gamma).inv.app D).left)
    72	      (𝟙 D.left) := h
    73	  rw [Category.id_comp] at hfixed
    74	  exact hfixed
    75	
    76	/-- The `K`-slice deck transformation indexed by `gamma⁻¹` is the restriction
    77	of the `L`-slice deck transformation indexed by `gamma`, after the canonical
    78	identity-underlying comparison of their sources. -/
    79	theorem twistTest_eq_pic0GaloisRestrict_galTwistMor
    80	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) (gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
    81	    twistTest T gamma⁻¹ =
    82	      (pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso gamma).inv.app (baseTest (k' := L) T) ≫
    83	        (pic0GaloisRestrictTest (k := K) (L := L)).map
    84	          (pic0GalTwistMor T gamma) := by
    85	  apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
    86	  rw [Over.comp_left, pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso_inv_app_left,
    87	    Over.map_map_left, pic0GalTwistMor_left]
    88	  have hfixed : @Eq
    89	      (Limits.pullback T.hom (specMapAlgebra K L) ⟶
    90	        Limits.pullback T.hom (specMapAlgebra K L))
    91	      (𝟙 _ ≫ pullbackGalMap K L T.hom gamma)
    92	      (pullbackGalMap K L T.hom gamma) :=
    93	    Category.id_comp _
    94	  exact hfixed.symm
    95	
    96	/-! ## Transporting deck invariance through theta -/
    97	
    98	section ThetaAction
    99	
   100	variable (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
   101	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   102	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   103	
   104	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
   105	-- Normalizing both theta components and the restriction-twist inverse is expensive.
   106	/-- The theta comparison carries invariance under the inverse-indexed deck
   107	transformation to the canonical Galois-action equation. -/
   108	theorem pic0_theta_invariant_iff_action
   109	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
   110	    (y : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange K L).obj C)).obj
   111	      (op (baseTest (k' := L) T)))
   112	    (gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
   113	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (twistTest T gamma⁻¹).op
   114	          ((pic0ThetaType K L C).hom.app
   115	            (op (baseTest (k' := L) T)) y) =
   116	        (pic0ThetaType K L C).hom.app
   117	          (op (baseTest (k' := L) T)) y ↔
   118	      (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange K L).obj C)).map
   119	          (pic0GalTwistMor T gamma).op y =
   120	        (pic0GaloisAction C gamma).inv.app
   121	          (op (baseTest (k' := L) T)) y := by
   122	  constructor
   123	  · intro h
   124	    rw [twistTest_eq_pic0GaloisRestrict_galTwistMor,
   125	      op_comp, Functor.map_comp] at h
   126	    have he : (pic0TypeFunctor C).map
   127	          ((pic0GaloisRestrictTest (k := K) (L := L)).map
   128	            (pic0GalTwistMor T gamma)).op
   129	          ((pic0ThetaType K L C).hom.app
   130	            (op (baseTest (k' := L) T)) y) =
   131	        (pic0TypeFunctor C).map
   132	          ((pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso gamma).hom.app
   133	            (baseTest (k' := L) T)).op
   134	          ((pic0ThetaType K L C).hom.app
   135	            (op (baseTest (k' := L) T)) y) := by
   136	      calc
   137	        _ = (pic0TypeFunctor C).map
   138	            ((pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso gamma).hom.app
   139	              (baseTest (k' := L) T)).op
   140	            ((pic0TypeFunctor C).map
   141	              ((pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso gamma).inv.app
   142	                (baseTest (k' := L) T)).op
   143	              ((pic0TypeFunctor C).map
   144	                ((pic0GaloisRestrictTest (k := K) (L := L)).map
   145	                  (pic0GalTwistMor T gamma)).op
   146	                ((pic0ThetaType K L C).hom.app
   147	                  (op (baseTest (k' := L) T)) y))) := by
   148	            symm
   149	            rw [← CategoryTheory.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp,
   150	              Iso.hom_inv_id_app]
   151	            simpa using Functor.map_id_apply (pic0TypeFunctor C)
   152	              (op ((pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma ⋙
   153	                pic0GaloisRestrictTest).obj (baseTest (k' := L) T))) _
   154	        _ = _ := congrArg ((pic0TypeFunctor C).map
   155	          ((pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso gamma).hom.app
   156	            (baseTest (k' := L) T)).op) h
   157	    apply (Iso.toEquiv ((pic0ThetaType K L C).app
   158	      (op ((pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).obj
   159	        (baseTest (k' := L) T))))).injective
   160	    change (pic0ThetaType K L C).hom.app
   161	        (op ((pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).obj (baseTest (k' := L) T)))
   162	          ((pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange K L).obj C)).map
   163	            (pic0GalTwistMor T gamma).op y) =
   164	      (pic0ThetaType K L C).hom.app
   165	        (op ((pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).obj (baseTest (k' := L) T)))
   166	          ((pic0GaloisAction C gamma).inv.app

# AlgebraicJacobian (rebuild)

<!-- archon:readme -->

## Project

A **from-scratch rebuild** of the Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of the **Jacobian of a smooth,
proper, geometrically irreducible curve** over a field (Christian Merten's AI challenge, inspired by
Kevin Buzzard's Riemann-surface version). By a smooth curve we mean a geometrically irreducible,
smooth scheme of relative dimension one over a field.

This project supplies the missing definitions (`genus`, `Jacobian`, the Abel–Jacobi map `ofCurve`)
and theorems (the Jacobian is smooth of relative dimension equal to the genus, proper, geometrically
irreducible, and is the Albanese variety of the curve, characterized by the universal property
`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`). It targets the **extended** challenge: additionally, the Jacobian is
**functorial** in the curve (`Jacobian.functor`) and **commutes with base change of fields**
(`baseChangeIso` with identity and cocycle coherences, and Abel–Jacobi compatibility
`baseChange_ofCurve`), which makes the construction canonical.

It is rebuilt rather than continued: the goal is a cleaner, more general, mathlib-idiomatic
infrastructure and a shorter, clearer path to the conclusion. The existing project
`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` may be **read** when genuinely blocked, but nothing is
copied from it — every declaration is rewritten. The rebuild is driven by its Archon Horizon task,
which carries the full charter (target, constraints, working model, and phases).

## Structure

- `AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` — the single, reviewable **statement file**: every signature a
  reviewer must trust, and nothing else. Agents own the proofs, never these signatures.
- `AlgebraicJacobian/` — the infrastructure that discharges the statement (added as the rebuild
  proceeds; the 500-line-per-file house rule and its current over-limit set are tracked and
  re-measured in inbox `I-0220`; layout mirrors the mathematical structure of the paper).
- `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — the library root import list, and the index of what is actually
  checked: `lake build`'s default target is this module, so a new file is **not** elaborated by a
  bare `lake build` until it is imported here. Add the import, or check the file explicitly by
  module name. Reachability is a moving target while parallel lanes add files and imports:
  measure it **transitively** from the current root rather than quoting a stale count. See roadmap
  row `AJCR.w4-rep.build-reach` for the triaged list, and check the root before trusting a "landed"
  claim.
- `informal/` — 79 design worksheets, brick specs, and recon dumps (~32k lines). **Start from
  [`informal/README.md`](informal/README.md)**, which says what each file is for and which are
  superseded; several are pinned to routes that have since been abandoned.
- `blueprint/` — a clean **mathematical** blueprint (no Lean code in the prose; nodes carry `\lean{}`
  and `\source{}` anchors). Build with `leanblueprint pdf` / `leanblueprint web`.
- `archon-protected.yaml` — the mathematician-owned signatures agents must not modify.

## Sources

The shared workspace-root [`references/`](../../references/) library (indexed by
`references/manifest.yaml`) backs the blueprint. Read a source before citing it with `\source{...}`.

## How to build

```bash
lake build           # compile (olean cache shared via ../../.lake-packages)
```
# `informal/` — index of design worksheets, specs, and recon dumps

80 files, ~32k lines. This index exists so a new session can tell **which file is still
authoritative** without reading them. Created 2026-07-27 (janitor pass, run 0048 round 5);
re-reconciled against the directory 2026-08-06 (janitor pass, run 0122).

**How the status column was derived — read this before trusting it.** Each entry's title comes
from reading the file's header. `SUPERSEDED-BY` is recorded **only** where the file itself (or its
successor) says so in writing; it was not inferred from dates. `LANDED` means the roadmap wave the
file serves is `done`, so the file is a historical record of shipped work, not a live instruction.
The ~27k lines were *not* read end to end — a `CURRENT` mark means "no evidence of supersession was
found", not "audited line by line".

**Two standing cautions that apply to every file here.**

- **Line references drift.** These worksheets cite `File.lean:NNN` heavily and the citations are
  not maintained. Always re-locate by name, never by line number.
- **A worksheet naming a declaration is not evidence it exists** (inbox `I-0349`). Worksheets
  *reserve* names for bricks not yet built. Before claiming one, read the signature the worksheet
  gives it (inbox `I-0354`) and check the tree with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<name>" --json`.

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageAffineBaseChange
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageGluingBaseChange
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Naturality of finite-stage Picard restrictions after base change
    11	
    12	The restriction legs in a finite-stage glue package are affine morphisms over the
    13	final finite subextension.  Their pullbacks to the separably closed field agree,
    14	under the final ring comparisons, with the canonical restrictions in the exact
    15	Picard atlas.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	
    20	universe u
    21	
    22	open CategoryTheory Limits TensorProduct
    23	open scoped TensorProduct
    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    26	
    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    30	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    31	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    32	
    33	namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    34	
    35	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    36	-- Projecting the package unfolds the dependent finite-subextension towers.
    37	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    38	/-- The left restriction leg of the glue package is the spectrum of the
    39	scalar-extended descended restriction. -/
    40	theorem glueData_f
    41	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    42	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
    43	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    44	    P.glueData.f U V =
    45	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    46	        (pic0FiniteStageRestrictionBaseChange
    47	          C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N U V).toRingHom) := by
    48	  rfl
    49	
    50	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    51	-- The annotation fixes the source and target instances hidden by dependent indices.
    52	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    53	/-- The scalar-extended descended restriction, with its chart and overlap types
    54	fixed opaquely for use by the affine base-change API. -/
    55	noncomputable def restrictionBaseChangeAlgHom
    56	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    57	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
    58	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    59	    Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing
    60	        C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U →ₐ[P.N.1]
    61	      Pic0FiniteStageOverlapBaseChangeRing
    62	        C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U V :=
    63	  (pic0FiniteStageRestrictionBaseChange
    64	      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N U V :
    65	    Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing
    66	        C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U →ₐ[P.N.1]
    67	      Pic0FiniteStageOverlapBaseChangeRing
    68	        C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U V)
    69	
    70	/-- The exact left restriction with indexed source and target rings.  Keeping
    71	the indexed rings avoids relying on typeclass transparency for their aliases. -/
    72	noncomputable def exactRestrictionAlgHom
    73	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    74	    Pic0FiniteStageRing C (Sum.inl U) →ₐ[k]
    75	      Pic0FiniteStageRing C (Sum.inr (U, V)) :=
    76	  pic0FiniteStageMap C (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (U, V)))
    77	
    78	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    79	-- The annotation fixes the indexed exact-ring instance on the chart target.
    80	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    81	/-- Final scalar-extension comparison for a chart, with an indexed exact-ring
    82	target. -/
    83	noncomputable def chartFinalBaseChangeEquiv
    84	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    85	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
    86	    (U : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    87	    k ⊗[P.N.1]
    88	        Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing
    89	          C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U ≃ₐ[k]
    90	      Pic0FiniteStageRing C (Sum.inl U) :=
    91	  pic0FiniteStageFinalBaseChangeEquiv
    92	    C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.e P.M P.N (Sum.inl U)
    93	
    94	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    95	-- The annotation fixes the indexed exact-ring instance on the overlap target.
    96	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    97	/-- Final scalar-extension comparison for an overlap, with an indexed
    98	exact-ring target. -/
    99	noncomputable def overlapFinalBaseChangeEquiv
   100	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
   101	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
   102	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
   103	    k ⊗[P.N.1]
   104	        Pic0FiniteStageOverlapBaseChangeRing
   105	          C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U V ≃ₐ[k]
   106	      Pic0FiniteStageRing C (Sum.inr (U, V)) :=
   107	  pic0FiniteStageFinalBaseChangeEquiv
   108	    C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.e P.M P.N (Sum.inr (U, V))
   109	
   110	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
   111	-- Specializing the generic pullback map infers both scalar-extended model rings.
   112	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
   113	/-- Pullback of a finite-stage left restriction from an overlap to its left
   114	chart. -/
   115	noncomputable def restrictionBaseChangeMap
   116	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
   117	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
   118	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
   119	    pullback
   120	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
   121	          (algebraMap P.N.1
   122	            (Pic0FiniteStageOverlapBaseChangeRing
   123	              C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U V))))
   124	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k))) ⟶
   125	      pullback
   126	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
   127	          (algebraMap P.N.1
   128	            (Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing
   129	              C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U))))
   130	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k))) :=
   131	  affineBaseChangeMap P.N.1 k
   132	    (Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing
   133	      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U)
   134	    (Pic0FiniteStageOverlapBaseChangeRing
   135	      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U V)
   136	    (restrictionBaseChangeAlgHom C P U V)
   137	
   138	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
   139	-- The chart comparison cancels the package's nested scalar extensions.
   140	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
   141	/-- The tensor-product and final-ring comparison for a chart, before applying
   142	the chart's affine-open identification. -/
   143	noncomputable def chartRingBaseChangeIso
   144	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
   145	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
   146	    (U : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
   147	    pullback
   148	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
   149	          (algebraMap P.N.1
   150	            (Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing
   151	              C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U))))
   152	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k))) ≅
   153	      Spec (.of (Pic0FiniteStageRing C (Sum.inl U))) :=
   154	  affineBaseChangeIso P.N.1 k
   155	      (Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing
   156	        C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U) ≪≫
   157	    Scheme.Spec.mapIso
   158	      (chartFinalBaseChangeEquiv C P U).symm.toRingEquiv.toCommRingCatIso.op
   159	
   160	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
   161	-- The overlap comparison cancels the package's nested scalar extensions.
   162	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
   163	/-- The tensor-product and final-ring comparison for an overlap, before applying
   164	the overlap's affine-open identification. -/
   165	noncomputable def overlapRingBaseChangeIso
   166	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
   167	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
   168	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
   169	    pullback
   170	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
   171	          (algebraMap P.N.1
   172	            (Pic0FiniteStageOverlapBaseChangeRing
   173	              C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U V))))
   174	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k))) ≅
   175	      Spec (.of (Pic0FiniteStageRing C (Sum.inr (U, V)))) :=
   176	  affineBaseChangeIso P.N.1 k
   177	      (Pic0FiniteStageOverlapBaseChangeRing
   178	        C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U V) ≪≫
   179	    Scheme.Spec.mapIso
   180	      (overlapFinalBaseChangeEquiv
   181	        C P U V).symm.toRingEquiv.toCommRingCatIso.op
   182	
   183	end Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
   184	
   185	end
   186	
   187	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChange

     8	/-!
     9	# Naturality of affine scalar extension
    10	
    11	For an algebra map A -> B, base change carries Spec B -> Spec A to the
    12	contravariant Spec of the scalar-extended algebra map.  The tensor factors are
    13	ordered with the extension ring on the left, matching the finite-stage Picard
    14	ring comparisons.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory Limits TensorProduct
    22	open scoped TensorProduct
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    29	
    30	variable (R K A B : Type u)
    31	variable [CommRing R] [CommRing K] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    32	variable [Algebra R K] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    33	
    34	/-- The affine base-change isomorphism with the extension ring as the left
    35	tensor factor. -/
    36	noncomputable def affineBaseChangeIso :
    37	    pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R A)))
    38	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))) ≅
    39	      Spec (.of (K ⊗[R] A)) :=
    40	  pullbackSymmetry _ _ ≪≫ pullbackSpecIso R K A
    41	
    42	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
    43	theorem affineBaseChangeIso_inv_fst :
    44	    (affineBaseChangeIso R K A).inv ≫ pullback.fst _ _ =
    45	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    46	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
    47	          A →ₐ[R] K ⊗[R] A).toRingHom) := by
    48	  simp [affineBaseChangeIso]
    49	
    50	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
    51	theorem affineBaseChangeIso_inv_snd :
    52	    (affineBaseChangeIso R K A).inv ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
    53	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    54	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom :
    55	          K →+* K ⊗[R] A)) := by
    56	  simp [affineBaseChangeIso]
    57	
    58	/-- Base change of an affine morphism over Spec R. -/
    59	noncomputable def affineBaseChangeMap (phi : A →ₐ[R] B) :
    60	    pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R B)))
    61	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))) ⟶
    62	      pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R A)))
    63	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))) :=
    64	  pullback.map _ _ _ _
    65	    (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom phi.toRingHom)) (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _)
    66	    (by
    67	      rw [Category.comp_id, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    68	      congr 2
    69	      exact phi.comp_algebraMap.symm)
    70	    (by simp)
    71	
    72	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
    73	theorem affineBaseChangeMap_fst (phi : A →ₐ[R] B) :
    74	    affineBaseChangeMap R K A B phi ≫ pullback.fst _ _ =
    75	      pullback.fst _ _ ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom phi.toRingHom) := by
    76	  unfold affineBaseChangeMap
    77	  exact pullback.lift_fst _ _ _
    78	
    79	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
    80	theorem affineBaseChangeMap_snd (phi : A →ₐ[R] B) :
    81	    affineBaseChangeMap R K A B phi ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
    82	      pullback.snd _ _ := by
    83	  unfold affineBaseChangeMap
    84	  rw [pullback.lift_snd]
    85	  simp
    86	
    87	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    88	-- Both pullback projections expand tensor-product universal maps.
    89	/-- The affine base-change isomorphisms intertwine a base-changed morphism with
    90	the Spec of its scalar extension. -/
    91	theorem affineBaseChangeIso_naturality (phi : A →ₐ[R] B) :
    92	    affineBaseChangeMap R K A B phi ≫ (affineBaseChangeIso R K A).hom =
    93	      (affineBaseChangeIso R K B).hom ≫
    94	        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    95	          (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
    96	            (R := R) (K := K) phi).toRingHom) := by
    97	  rw [← cancel_epi (affineBaseChangeIso R K B).inv]
    98	  simp only [Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
    99	  rw [← cancel_mono (affineBaseChangeIso R K A).inv]
   100	  simp only [Category.assoc, Iso.hom_inv_id, Category.comp_id]
   101	  apply pullback.hom_ext
   102	  · rw [Category.assoc, affineBaseChangeMap_fst]
   103	    simp only [Category.assoc]
   104	    rw [affineBaseChangeIso_inv_fst_assoc (R := R) (K := K) (A := B)]
   105	    rw [affineBaseChangeIso_inv_fst (R := R) (K := K) (A := A)]
   106	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
   107	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
   108	    congr 2
   109	  · rw [Category.assoc, affineBaseChangeMap_snd]
   110	    simp only [Category.assoc]
   111	    rw [affineBaseChangeIso_inv_snd (R := R) (K := K) (A := B)]
   112	    rw [affineBaseChangeIso_inv_snd (R := R) (K := K) (A := A)]
   113	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
   114	    congr 2
   115	    ext x
   116	    simp [AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom]
   117	
   118	end Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
   119	
   120	end
   121	
   122	end AlgebraicGeometry

    45	  let A : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Type u := fun U =>

    15	
    16	/-!
    17	# Representability of schemes is a local property
    18	
    19	In this file we prove that a sheaf of types `F` on `Sch` is representable if it is
    20	locally representable.
    21	
    22	## Main result
    23	- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalRepresentability.isRepresentable`:
    24	  Suppose
    25	  * F is a `Type u`-valued sheaf on `Sch` with respect to the Zariski topology
    26	  * X : ι → Sch is a family of schemes
    27	  * f : Π i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ F is a family of relatively representable open immersions
    28	  * f is jointly surjective
    29	
    30	  Then `F` is representable.
    31	
    32	## References
    33	* https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01JJ
    34	
    35	-/
    36	
    37	@[expose] public section
    38	
    39	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    40	
    41	open CategoryTheory Category Limits Opposite
    42	
    43	universe u
    44	
    45	namespace Scheme
    46	
    47	/-
    48	Consider the following setup:
    49	* F is `Type u`-valued a sheaf on `Sch` with respect to the Zariski topology
    50	* X : ι → Sch is a family of schemes
    51	* f : Π i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ F is a family of relatively representable open immersions
    52	
    53	Later, we will also assume:
    54	* The family f is locally surjective with respect to the Zariski topology
    55	-/
    56	variable (F : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u))
    57	  {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    58	  (f : (i : ι) → yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ F.1) (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
    59	
    60	namespace LocalRepresentability
    61	
    62	variable {F f} (i j k : ι)
    63	
    64	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
    65	open Functor.relativelyRepresentable in
    66	/-- We get a family of gluing data by taking `U i = X i` and `V i j = (hf i).rep.pullback (f j)`. -/
    67	@[simps]

          "body": "THIRD-LANE CONFIRMATION, plus a tripwire one line CHEAPER than step 2: COMMIT'S OWN STAT LINE DISAGREES WITH THE PRE-COMMIT STAT.\n\najcr-p2 r6, commit 7e90a01d09, reverted in 85e042e6f0. I followed step 1 exactly -- fresh index (rm -f), read-tree HEAD, add 2 explicit paths, verified name-status listed exactly those 2 and shortstat read '2 files changed, 212 insertions(+)', ZERO deletions. Then commit printed:\n\n  3 files changed, 226 insertions(+), 46 DELETIONS(-)\n\n2 vs 3, 0 vs 46 -- printed by commit itself, no extra command. So: READ THE STAT COMMIT PRINTS AND COMPARE IT TO THE ONE YOU JUST VERIFIED. Step 2 is still needed to name the path; the mismatch is visible earlier and free.\n\nWHAT I CLOBBERED: ajc-p1's Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/.../GaloisDescent/GaloisSelfTensor.lean, reverted 306 -> 274 lines. Disk still held their version (sha256 03d1fd0fc6.., byte-identical to HEAD~2); restored in 85e042e6f0 and verified HEAD == disk afterwards. Out of HEAD for one commit, never lost.\n\nMY WINDOW WAS UNDER A MINUTE -- read-tree, one add, two checks, commit. With 8 runs live this is not fixable by being quick, only by checking after."

          "body": "SECOND INSTANCE, same session, same lane (ajcr-p2 r6) -- and it SHARPENS what the tripwire is about.\n\nCommit f246e1d285, reverted in 82460ebba9. Victim: ajc-p1's AJC PicEtDescentRepresentability.lean, 159 -> 119 lines, restored byte-identical (sha256 935b4274b1c0ae7a == disk == HEAD~2). My payload was TWO ROADMAP FILES. Pre-commit stat: 2 files, 30 insertions, 1 deletion. Commit printed: 3 files, 30 insertions, 41 DELETIONS.\n\nTHE SHARPENING: my first clobber this session was a Lean-file commit, this one a roadmap-file commit. NEITHER payload touched the victim's project. So the race is not about what you are committing, how large it is, or which project it is in -- it is purely about elapsed time between read-tree and commit, and roadmap/inbox commits are just as dangerous as .lean ones. A lane that applies the fresh-index discipline only to proof commits is unprotected exactly half the time.\n\nThe stat comparison caught both within seconds. I now run it on every commit including board and inbox ones."

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

    11	
    12	Representability turns the fixed-base Picard-zero functor into the functor of morphisms to its
    13	representing scheme.  If that scheme is locally of finite presentation, the scheme-theoretic
    14	finite-stage factorization and equality theorems show that this functor preserves the filtered
    15	colimits occurring in `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`.

    26	/-- A locally finitely presented scheme representing `pic0TypeFunctor C` discharges the
    27	fixed-base filtered-colimit residual `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C`. -/

    31	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

    37	  let D := S ⋙ Over.forget (Spec (.of k))
    38	  let t : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj (Spec (.of k)) :=
    39	    { app := fun i => (S.obj i).hom
    40	      naturality := fun {i j} f => by
    41	        change (S.map f).left ≫ (S.obj j).hom = (S.obj i).hom ≫ 𝟙 _
    42	        rw [Category.comp_id]
    43	        exact Over.w (S.map f) }
    44	  let c : Cone D := (Over.forget (Spec (.of k))).mapCone (limit.cone S)
    45	  have hc : IsLimit c :=
    46	    isLimitOfPreserves (Over.forget (Spec (.of k))) (limit.isLimit S)
    47	  letI {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j) : IsAffineHom (D.map f) := h_aff f
    48	  letI (i : I) : CompactSpace (D.obj i) := hcompact i
    49	  letI (i : I) : QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i) := hqs i
    50	  refine preservesColimit_of_preserves_colimit_cocone
    51	    (K := S.op) (F := pic0TypeFunctor C) (limit.isLimit S).op ?_
    52	  refine Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf' (S.op ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor C)
    53	    ((pic0TypeFunctor C).mapCocone (limit.cone S).op) ?_ ?_
    54	  · intro x
    55	    let a : limit S ⟶ J := rep.homEquiv.symm x
    56	    have ha : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const I).map (a.left ≫ J.hom) := by
    57	      ext i
    58	      change (limit.π S i).left ≫ (S.obj i).hom = a.left ≫ J.hom
    59	      rw [Over.w (limit.π S i), Over.w a]
    60	    obtain ⟨i, g, hg, hgbase⟩ :=
    61	      Scheme.exists_π_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation
    62	        D t J.hom c hc a.left ha

    65	    change x = (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (limit.π S i).op (rep.homEquiv g')

    81	      exact hxy

    85	/-- **The DG-G0.δ index** — the finite subextensions `k''` of a separable algebraic extension
    86	`K/k`, ordered by inclusion.  Its directed supremum is `K` (`iSup_finSubext_eq_top`); its
    87	opposite is the `IsCofiltered` shape the β1 residual `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`
    88	quantifies over.  For `K = K_s` a separable closure these are exactly the *finite separable*
    89	subextensions of `K_s/k`. -/
    90	abbrev FinSubext : Type u := {L : IntermediateField k K // FiniteDimensional k L}
    91	
    92	variable {k K}
    93	
    94	/-- Each stage carries its finite-dimensionality as an instance. -/
    95	instance (L : FinSubext k K) : FiniteDimensional k L.1 := L.2
    96	
    97	variable (k K) in
    98	/-- The δ index is nonempty (`k` itself, as `⊥`, is a finite subextension). -/
    99	instance instNonemptyFinSubext [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] : Nonempty (FinSubext k K) :=
   100	  ⟨⟨k⟮(0 : K)⟯, adjoin.finiteDimensional (Algebra.IsIntegral.isIntegral _)⟩⟩
   101	
   102	/-- **DG-G0.δ, directedness.**  The finite subextensions of `K/k` are directed under inclusion:
   103	the join `k'' ⊔ k'''` of two finite subextensions is again finite.  Hence `(FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ` is
   104	`IsCofiltered` — the shape the residual consumes. -/
   105	theorem directed_finSubext :
   106	    Directed (· ≤ ·) (fun L : FinSubext k K => (L.1 : IntermediateField k K)) := by
   107	  intro L₁ L₂
   108	  haveI := L₁.2
   109	  haveI := L₂.2
   110	  exact ⟨⟨L₁.1 ⊔ L₂.1, IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_sup _ _⟩, le_sup_left, le_sup_right⟩
   111	
   112	/-- **DG-G0.δ, `IsDirected`.**  The δ index is a directed order (from `directed_finSubext`), so it
   113	is `IsFiltered` and its opposite `(FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ` is `IsCofiltered` — automatically, via
   114	`isFiltered_of_directed_le_nonempty` and `isCofiltered_op_of_isFiltered`. -/
   115	instance instIsDirectedFinSubext [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] :
   116	    IsDirected (FinSubext k K) (· ≤ ·) :=
   117	  ⟨fun L₁ L₂ => directed_finSubext L₁ L₂⟩
   118	
   119	/-- **DG-G0.δ, the cofiltered shape the residual consumes.**  `(FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ` is
   120	`IsCofiltered` — exactly the `[IsCofiltered J]` shape of `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`'s
   121	diagram binder.  A cofiltered diagram of test schemes `S : (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Over (Spec k)`
   122	indexed by it — in particular the `Spec`-of-tests limit `S_{K_s} = lim_{k''} S_{k''}` (with
   123	affine transition maps `Spec k''' → Spec k''` and one-point, hence compact and quasi-separated,
   124	stages) — is therefore a legal input to the β1 residual. -/
   125	instance instIsCofilteredFinSubextOp [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] :
   126	    IsCofiltered (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ :=
   127	  inferInstance
   128	
   129	/-- **DG-G0.δ, the colimit at the lattice level: `K = colim k''`.**  For an algebraic extension
   130	`K/k` the supremum of the finite subextensions is all of `K`: every `x : K` is algebraic, hence
   131	lies in the finite subextension `k⟮x⟯`. -/
   132	theorem iSup_finSubext_eq_top [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] :
   133	    ⨆ L : FinSubext k K, (L.1 : IntermediateField k K) = ⊤ :=
   134	  le_top.antisymm fun x _ =>
   135	    le_iSup (fun L : FinSubext k K => (L.1 : IntermediateField k K))
   136	      ⟨k⟮x⟯, adjoin.finiteDimensional (Algebra.IsIntegral.isIntegral x)⟩ <|
   137	      mem_adjoin_simple_self k x
   138	
   139	/-- **DG-G0.δ, colimit-is-union.**  The directed supremum of the finite subextensions is their
   140	set-theoretic **union** (`IntermediateField.coe_iSup_of_directed`): the honest "`K_s = colim k''`"
   141	statement.  Combined with `iSup_finSubext_eq_top`, every element of `K` already lives at a finite
   142	stage `k''`. -/
   143	theorem coe_iSup_finSubext [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] :
   144	    (↑(⨆ L : FinSubext k K, (L.1 : IntermediateField k K)) : Set K)
   145	      = ⋃ L : FinSubext k K, (L.1 : Set K) :=
   146	  IntermediateField.coe_iSup_of_directed directed_finSubext
   147	
   148	/-- **DG-G0.δ, separability of each stage.**  Every finite subextension `k''/k` of a separable
   149	extension `K/k` is itself separable (`Algebra.isSeparable_tower_bot_of_isSeparable` on the native
   150	tower `k → k'' → K`).  With `IntermediateField.isSeparable_iSup` the colimit `⨆ k''` is separable,
   151	so the δ system is the directed system of *finite separable* subextensions. -/
   152	instance isSeparable_finSubext [Algebra.IsSeparable k K] (L : FinSubext k K) :
   153	    Algebra.IsSeparable k L.1 :=
   154	  Algebra.isSeparable_tower_bot_of_isSeparable k L.1 K
   155	
   156	end FieldSystem
